name: sol_defi_as_13
description: On-chain slippage/minimum-output calculation manipulable via price oracle or reserves
question: The source file in `source` implements a swap or liquidity function that computes its own minimum-acceptable output or slippage bound internally from current on-chain reserves, spot price, or oracle values (e.g., expectedOut derived from getReserves/price feed minus a fixed percent) rather than accepting a caller-supplied minAmountOut/maxSlippage parameter calculated off-chain, so an attacker can manipulate the on-chain price/reserves in the same transaction to widen or narrow the computed bound and extract value; this excludes functions that accept an explicit user- or off-chain-supplied minOut/maxIn parameter and simply validate against it.
criteria: swap() computes minOut = getAmountOut(reserveIn, reserveOut, amountIn) * (100 - slippageBps) / 100 using live pool reserves instead of a caller-supplied minOut parameter
addLiquidity() derives the acceptable price range from the pair's current spot price fetched on-chain immediately before the check, with no user-supplied minPrice/maxPrice
function calculates expectedAmount from oracle.getPrice() and reverts if actualAmount deviates more than a hardcoded percent, with no external minAmountOut argument
removeLiquidity() computes minTokenOut internally from totalSupply and reserves ratio at call time rather than accepting a caller-provided minimum
